then.text: Walton split the atom and then spent forty years teaching undergraduates to do sums. Both are hard. I know which I find harder.
All four! Boyle's gas, Walton's atom, Lonsdale's flat ring and Bell Burnell's pulsar. And mostly they had to leave Ireland to do it.
Walton came home, mind, and taught here for decades. Have these, and tell people about them. That's the whole job of a plaque.

else.text: How's the hunt? Boyle and Walton are on plaques in the Comeraghs, County Waterford. Bell Burnell's by Lough Neagh, and Lonsdale's here in Dublin.

Professor Brennan, physics. Ernest Walton taught in this college for decades, and half of Dublin walks past without knowing he split the atom.

Ireland has a few scientists the world forgot to mention. Find me four: Boyle and Walton on plaques in the Comeraghs, Jocelyn Bell Burnell by Lough Neagh, and Kathleen Lonsdale on a plaque here in Dublin.

dub_trinity_librarian.text: Quietly, if you will. The Book of Kells is a copy of the four Gospels, made around the year 800 by monks. It came to Trinity in 1661.
The Long Room is 65 metres, with 200,000 old books and a smell students call 'academic'. It gives every visitor goosebumps.
Our oldest harp is the model for the harp on Irish coins. It is about 600 years old and has not played a note in ages.
